disease_label_per_paper: Acute rheumatic fever with migratory arthritis, erythematous plaques, and subcutaneous nodules
presentation_summary: 32-year-old woman first presented to the emergency department with 54 hours of lower-extremity pain and swelling, worse in the left knee for 48 hours, without trauma.

She reported prior similar pain in elbows and ankles that had subsided with over-the-counter NSAIDs. At first visit she was afebrile with normal blood pressure, pulse, and respiratory rate; exam showed left knee medial and lateral tenderness without systemic abnormalities.
Ten days later she returned with more severe pain in different joints, mostly ankles, wrists, and knees.
Exam at readmission showed blanching erythematous plaques most noticeable over trunk and back, and subcutaneous nodules on both arms. No murmur was heard and neurologic exam was normal.

WBC and ESR were elevated and hemoglobin was normal. Throat culture was negative. ASO/anti-DNase B elevation, infection/mimic testing, ECG/echo normality, and final diagnosis are kept as confirmatory/non-ranking context.
